label: Ownership
description: Rust's system for managing memory without a garbage collector, using rules of ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes.

label: Borrowing & References
description: Mechanism to allow safe access to data without taking ownership, including mutable and immutable references.

label: Enums & Pattern Matching
description: Enums define types with multiple variants; pattern matching allows exhaustive handling of these variants.

label: Traits
description: Define shared behavior across types, similar to interfaces in other languages, enabling polymorphism.

label: Generics
description: Enable writing functions, structs, and enums that can operate on different types without losing type safety.

label: Macros
description: Powerful metaprogramming feature for code generation and reducing boilerplate using declarative or procedural macros.

label: Error Handling
description: Rust encourages explicit error handling using Result and Option types, avoiding exceptions.

label: Concurrency
description: Rust ensures thread safety at compile-time, supporting threads, async/await, and message-passing concurrency.

label: Smart Pointers
description: Data structures like Box, Rc, Arc, and RefCell provide controlled heap allocation and shared ownership.

label: FFI (Foreign Function Interface)
description: Allows Rust code to interact safely with C or other languages, enabling integration with existing libraries.

label: Crates & Cargo
description: Rust's package manager (Cargo) and the ecosystem of libraries (crates) for dependency management and project building.

label: Modules & Packages
description: Organize code into modules and packages for better structure, encapsulation, and reusability.

label: Lifetimes
description: Annotate the scope during which references are valid to prevent dangling pointers and ensure memory safety.

label: Async Programming
description: Rust’s asynchronous model allows non-blocking execution using async/await and Futures.

label: Interior Mutability
description: Allows mutation of data even when a value is immutable using types like RefCell and Mutex.

label: Zero-Cost Abstractions
description: Rust aims to provide high-level abstractions that compile down to efficient machine code with no runtime overhead.

label: Unsafe Rust
description: Sections of Rust code that bypass some safety checks for low-level operations, requiring careful manual management.

label: Serde (Serialization/Deserialization)
description: Popular Rust framework for converting data structures to/from formats like JSON, TOML, or YAML.

label: Smart Pointers (Advanced)
description: Advanced patterns with Box, Rc, Arc, and Weak pointers to manage ownership, shared references, and cycles.

label: Embedded Rust
description: Using Rust for low-level programming on microcontrollers and constrained hardware with no standard library.

label: Const Generics
description: Allows defining types and functions parameterized by constant values, enabling more flexible and type-safe code.

label: Procedural Macros
description: Macros that generate code at compile-time using Rust functions, allowing powerful custom derives and attributes.

label: Pinning
description: Mechanism to prevent moving certain data in memory, crucial for async programming and self-referential structs.

label: Type Inference
description: Rust’s compiler can deduce types automatically, reducing boilerplate while keeping type safety.

label: Iterator & IntoIterator
description: Traits that allow creating, transforming, and consuming sequences of values efficiently.

label: Closures
description: Anonymous functions that can capture environment variables, supporting functional programming patterns.

label: Smart Error Handling with ? Operator
description: Simplifies propagating errors using the ? operator, improving readability over verbose match statements.

label: PhantomData
description: A marker type used to indicate ownership or type relationships without storing actual data.

label: Newtype Pattern
description: Wrapping existing types in a new type to add type safety or implement custom traits without affecting the original type.

label: Unsafe Traits
description: Traits that require careful manual implementation due to invariants that the compiler cannot check automatically.
